desc: Initial attempt with segment tree + parallel binary search was too slow and complex; switch to two-pointer with monotonic stack and Fenwick tree for efficiency.
Implement a monotonic stack where each entry stores (value, count, start_index) representing blocks of constant running maximum.
Use a segment tree with lazy propagation supporting range assignment to maintain the running max array M, and range sum queries for the total cost.

When expanding right endpoint, find the leftmost position in the current window that is ≥ nums[R], then assign the range from that position+1 to R to have running max nums[R] (or maintain via a more granular approach).

When shrinking left endpoint, simply remove the contribution of the leftmost position by subtracting its cost from the total and decrementing the running max pointer if it was the unique maximum for a range.
Alternatively, implement a segment tree that stores the "profile" (running max values) and supports range cost queries in O(log n) or O(log² n) using a merge sort tree.
Test with the provided examples: nums=[6,3,1,2,4,4], k=7 → 17; nums=[6,3,1,3,6], k=4 → 12.
Verify O(n log n) complexity for n up to 10^5, and handle edge cases (single elements, equal values, large k).
